A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WBMM research and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices A–O. Their equations, algorithms, four figures and 20 tables can be matched reliably; raster figure content was checked visually.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-1K, ADE20K and COCO experiments, operator and hardware benchmarks, ablations and learned-weight analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix ablations, hardware measurements and learned-weight analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same window partitioning, relative-position indexing, batched multiplication, cross-window mixing, caching and reparameterization procedures. Identifier formatting changes do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K classification, ADE20K segmentation and COCO detection, with the same operator benchmarks and GPU, CPU and edge-device scenarios. No evaluated dataset, task or domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including UniRepLKNet, DW-Std/DW-LKA, SLaK variants, Win7 Transformer and ConvNeXt-T. Revised descriptions of prior work do not change the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Training schedules, architectures, preprocessing, metrics, batch sizes, resolutions and precision settings remain unchanged. Both retain 300-epoch ImageNet training, 160k ADE20K iterations and 36-epoch COCO training. Section 2.2's revised implementation wording does not report a changed experimental setup.

E4.justification: The feature-extraction, window-interaction, architecture and hierarchical-reparameterization ablations in Tables 2–4 are unchanged, as are the padding ablation in Table 12, learned-weight analysis in Figure 4 and appendix scaling analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report ablation means and standard deviations over three runs, and five independent runs with IQR-based outlier removal for operator benchmarks. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and reported findings match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table 5 retains WBMM-T's 83.2% Top-1 accuracy, and Table 6 retains hierarchical Tiny/Small single-scale mIoU of 48.8/50.6. Reformatted plots and hardware tables contain the same results.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2, their proofs, Equations 1–9, the arithmetic-intensity reasoning and Appendix N's training–inference equivalence derivation are unchanged. Notation formatting and algorithm placement do not revise the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2 contributions and conclusion retain the same novelty, efficiency, accuracy and hardware-generalization claims, including the 7.8× receptive-field comparison and 1.31–1.88× training speedup.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 narrows the assertion that modern frameworks use implicit GEMM for depthwise convolution to the authors' tested PyTorch/cuDNN configuration. This qualifies the scope of one implementation-based explanation; the result interpretations and Appendix O limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access link, hardware information, hyperparameters, model specifications and implementation algorithms are retained. Implicit GEMM was already identified for the benchmarks in v1's Section 4.1 and Table 13, so the revised qualification supplies no new experimental setting.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 attributes structural reparameterization's introduction to ACNet and popularization to RepVGG, and replaces RepLKNet's stated large-to-small kernel conversion with small-branch fusion into the large kernel. Section 2.5 changes Swin's bias description from shared across heads to per-head. The cited works themselves remain the same.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect Sections 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5, alongside expanded affiliations and bibliographic and notation cleanup. The overall narrative and main-text/appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from raster to vector rendering; Figure 3 is reformatted, with its line-style explanation moved into the caption. Tables 16–17 are enlarged, and appendix headings and algorithm placement reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Section 2.2's qualification better matches the implementation statement to the reported tests. Section 2.5's per-head Swin description also agrees with the within-head distinction already present in Appendix H. Enlarged Tables 16–17 improve legibility. These are supported gains in precision and presentation, while the method, empirical evidence and theory remain unchanged.
